```{r}
part<- randhealth %>%
  group_by(zper, coins) %>%
  summarise(
    first_year = min(year, na.rm = TRUE),
    last_year = max(year, na.rm = TRUE),
    years_participated = n_distinct(year),
    skipped_year = last_year - first_year + 1 > years_participated,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(coins, zper)

# we identify people don't start at the same place, we found skipping is not a big issue
# if we want to do specifically 3 years this would be different

part %>% group_by(skipped_year) %>% summarise(n=n())
```

```{r}
# 1. Create dummy health data


# 2. Calculate attrition relative to the baseline year (Cumulative Attrition)
baseline_count <- length(unique(randhealth$zper[randhealth$year == min(randhealth$year)]))

attrition_baseline <- randhealth %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    active_participants = n_distinct(zper),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    lost_since_baseline = baseline_count - active_participants,
    attrition_rate_pct = (lost_since_baseline / baseline_count) * 100
  )

print(attrition_baseline)


```

We are trying to test wether treament affect attrition


$$
H_0:p_1=p_2=p_3=p_4=p_5
H_A: \text{At least one treatment group has a different attrition rate.}
$$

```{r}
set.seed(2026)
# wether some one tropped out or not
# g1 <- randhealth %>%
#   group_by(zper,coins) %>%
#   summarise(
#     last_year = max(year),
#   ) %>% ungroup() %>%
#   mutate(
#     attrition = as.numeric(last_year < max(randhealth$year))
#   )

#  until year 3
# this is more reasonable
# since after year 3 we dont know who is dropped by experiemental design who is not
g1 <- randhealth %>%
  filter(year <= 3) %>%
  group_by(zper, coins) %>%
  summarise(
    last_year = max(year),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    attrition = as.numeric(last_year < 3)
  )

g1 %>%
  group_by(coins) %>%
  summarise(
    total = n(),
    attrition = sum(attrition == 1),
    no_attrition = sum(attrition == 0),
    attrition_rate = mean(attrition),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# calculates the maximum absolute difference between any coinsurance group's attrition rate and the overall average attrition rate.
# question Are the attrition rates across coinsurance groups more different from the overall attrition rate than we would expect by random assignment?
# We use the maximum absolute difference because it measures the most extreme departure of any coinsurance group's attrition rate from the overall average attrition rate. If even this largest difference is not statistically significant compared with the randomization distribution, then we do not have sufficient evidence that any group has an unusually different attrition rate.

obs_diff <- max(abs(
  tapply(g1$attrition, g1$coins, mean) -
    mean(g1$attrition)
))

# We shuffle the coinsurance labels and ask:
# - In the first shuffle, which group is most different?
# - In the second shuffle, which group is most different? and so on
# We record the largest difference each time.
# random chance can make one of the group look unusually large
# Then we ask if our most  exetrme attrition observation is different from random
# we pick the mean since we are interested if any attrition is diffent from the overall a ttrition

M <- 5000
perm_diff <- numeric(M)
for (m in 1:M) {
  # randomy shuffle the treatments
  z <- sample(g1$coins)

  perm_diff[m] <- max(abs(
    tapply(g1$attrition, z, mean) -
      mean(g1$attrition)
  ))
}

round(c(
  observed = obs_diff,
  p_value = (1 + sum(perm_diff >= obs_diff)) / (length(perm_diff) + 1)
), 4)


```


```{r}
set.seed(2026)

groups <- sort(unique(g1$coins))
# all possible combinations
pairs <- combn(groups, 2)

M <- 5000
results <- tibble()

for (i in 1:ncol(pairs)) {
  # treatment A
  gA <- pairs[1, i]
  # treatment B
  gB <- pairs[2, i]
  # only the two trement to be considered at the moment
  dat <- g1 %>%
    filter(coins %in% c(gA, gB))
  # Observed difference
  obs_diff <- with(dat,
    mean(attrition[coins == gA]) -
    mean(attrition[coins == gB])
  )

  # Randomization test
  perm_diff <- numeric(M)

  for (m in 1:M) {
    z <- sample(dat$coins)
    # diifferences in mean attrition between two treatments
    # mean since it gives us the difference in attrition
    perm_diff[m] <-
      mean(dat$attrition[z == gA]) -
      mean(dat$attrition[z == gB])
  }
  
  #  A p-value of exactly 0 is logically impossible in a permutation test because we know at least one configuration can produce that result—the one we observed.

  p <- (1 + sum(abs(perm_diff) >= abs(obs_diff))) / (M + 1)

  results <- rbind(results, data.frame(
    group1 = gA,
    group2 = gB,
    observed_diff = obs_diff,
    p_value = p
  ))
}

# Adjust for 10 comparisons
results$p_adjusted <- p.adjust(results$p_value, method = "holm")

results
# dataset summary

```

## Fit model
```{r}
pois_mod <- glm(
  mdvis ~ coins + income + xage + female + educdec + black + mdeoff + pioff +offset(log(time)),
  family = poisson(link = "log"),
  data = randhealth
)

nb_mod <- MASS::glm.nb(
  mdvis ~ coins + income + xage + female + educdec + black + offset(log(time)),
  data = randhealth
)

summary(pois_mod)
summary(nb_mod)
```

# Test zero inflation to see if zero inflation model is needed


```{r check 2}
n_sims <- 500; n <- nrow(randhealth)
zero_p <- zero_nb <- max_p <- max_nb <- numeric(n_sims) # one value per simulated dataset
for (s in 1:n_sims) {
y_p <- rpois(n, lambda = fitted(pois_mod)) # a dataset from the Poisson fit
y_nb <- rnbinom(n, mu = fitted(nb_mod), size = nb_mod$theta) # one from the negative binomial fit
zero_p[s] <- mean(y_p == 0); max_p[s] <- max(y_p)
zero_nb[s] <- mean(y_nb == 0); max_nb[s] <- max(y_nb)
}
round(rbind(data = c(prop_zero = mean(randhealth$y == 0), max = max(randhealth$y)),
poisson = c(mean(zero_p), mean(max_p)), negbin = c(mean(zero_nb), mean(max_nb))), 4)


```


```{r check3, fig.width=9, fig.height=3.3, out.width="92%"}

# we used square root of n as the bin size
binned <- function(x, r, m =  142) {          # average residuals in bins of x, cut at its quantiles
  b <- cut(x, unique(quantile(x, 0:m / m)), include.lowest = TRUE)   # tied values stay in one bin
  data.frame(x = tapply(x, b, mean), r = tapply(r, b, mean),
             se = tapply(r, b, function(z) sd(z) / sqrt(length(z))))
}
binned_plot <- function(x, r, xlab, xlim = NULL, ylim = NULL) {   # drawn as arm::binnedplot does
    # Dynamically calculate ylim if not provided by the user
  
  bb <- binned(x, r)
  
  if (is.null(ylim)) {
    # Calculate the lowest and highest points including the error bars (± 2 * SE)
    lower_bounds <- bb$r - 2 * bb$se
    upper_bounds <- bb$r + 2 * bb$se
    
    # Pad the limits slightly (e.g., 10%) so points don't sit right on the edge
    y_min <- min(c(lower_bounds, 0)) # Includes 0 so the baseline is visible
    y_max <- max(upper_bounds)
    padding <- (y_max - y_min) * 0.1
    
    ylim <- c(y_min - padding, y_max + padding)
  }
  

  plot(bb$x, bb$r, type = "n", xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim, xlab = xlab, ylab = "average Pearson residual")
  abline(0, 0, lty = 2)
  lines(bb$x, bb$r + 2 * bb$se, col = "gray", lwd = 0.5); lines(bb$x, bb$r - 2 * bb$se, col = "gray", lwd = 0.5)
  points(bb$x, bb$r, pch = 19, cex = 0.5)
}
r_nb <- resid(nb_mod, type = "pearson")
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1))
binned_plot(fitted(nb_mod), r_nb, "fitted mean count", xlim = c(0, 6))
# needs fixing
# binned_plot(randhealth$, r_nb, "roach1 (pretreatment count)")
```

```{r check3}
# our own tests

# test for model fit in terms of performance
performance(pois_mod)
performance(nb_mod)

# graph probability integral test and persona residual tests



counts <- nb_mod$y
lambdas <- fitted(nb_mod)
rqr <- rep(NA, length(lambdas))
for(i in 1:length(lambdas)){
  ai <- ppois(counts[i]-1, lambda=lambdas[i])
  bi <- ppois(counts[i], lambda=lambdas[i])
  # this works even when ai=bi
  ui <- ai + runif(1) * (bi - ai)
  ui <- max(min(ui, 1-10^(-6)), 10^(-6))
  rqr[i] <- qnorm(ui)
}
pearson.ratio <- sum(residuals(nb_mod, type = "pearson")^2) / nb_mod$df.residual
p1 <- ggplot(data=tibble(lambda=lambdas,
                         e=rqr)) + 
  geom_hline(yintercept=0, linetype="dotted")+
  geom_point(aes(x=lambda, y=e)) +
  theme_bw()+
  xlab(bquote(lambda))+
  ylab("Randomized Quantile Residuals")
p2 <- ggplot(data=tibble(e=rqr)) +
  stat_qq(aes(sample=e)) +
  stat_qq_line(aes(sample=e)) +
  theme_bw() +
  ggtitle(paste("Dispersion Ratio =", round(pearson.ratio, 4)))
p1+p2
```
